get.description: Stored logins answer HTTP Basic and Digest challenges of downloads from their host. Passwords are never returned.

Streams events as Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream).

Each event is sent as:

    id: <bootID>-<seq>
    event: <type>            (e.g. task.progress, task.status)
    data: <JSON event>

The id combines a token identifying the daemon process with the bus sequence
number, so a reconnecting client's Last-Event-ID is only honoured by the same
daemon process. On reconnect with Last-Event-ID the missed events are replayed
before live events. A `reset` event (data `{"reason": "restart"|"gap"|"overflow"}`)
tells the client it missed events and must refetch the state it mirrors:
"restart" when the Last-Event-ID belongs to another daemon process, "gap" when
the replay is incomplete, "overflow" when the client read too slowly.
A ": ping" comment is sent periodically to keep proxies from closing the
connection.

get.description: Reports that the daemon is up, its version, and whether the presented bearer token (if any) is valid. Does not require authentication.
The global speed limit now in force (and the configured one when a temporary override replaces it), the active speed profile, the quota usage of the global scope, and the same per queue.
get.summary: Speed limits and quotas in force

delete.description: Ends a temporary global speed override now; without one it does nothing. Answers like get-limits.

post.description: Replaces the global speed limit by speedLimit (0: unlimited, "turbo") for 1 to 1440 minutes; the configured limit and profiles apply again afterwards. A new override replaces the previous one. Clients are told with a limits.changed event, also when the override ends.
post.summary: Temporarily replace the global speed limit

get.description: Plugins are JavaScript extensions that resolve links, refresh expired links and react to downloads starting, failing and completing.

post.description: Copies a plugin from a directory, or clones it from a git repository, checks its manifest and script, and starts it. A plugin runs inside the daemon and may contact the hosts its manifest lists: install only plugins you trust.

delete.description: Removes the plugin, its files and the data it stored.

patch.summary: Switch a plugin on or off

Probes a URL or source with the effective settings and returns what would be downloaded (name, size, range support). The result is cached under resolveId, which create-task accepts until expiresAt. A failed probe returns 502 with the engine error code.

Probes up to 100 sources, a few at a time, and answers one result per item (200 even when some failed). Each success has a resolveId like resolve-task, and duplicateOf when another task already has the link or the file name and size.

patch.description: Changes name, dir, priority, labels (replaced as a whole; {} removes them) and/or settings overrides. settings is an RFC 7396 merge patch: null unsets a field. Name and dir cannot change while the task is active or has partial data (409).

Changes which files of a multi-file task (a torrent) are downloaded, also after it was created. The task's size follows the selection and the next run downloads exactly the selected files; files already downloaded and no longer selected stay on disk. Active and completed tasks cannot change (409 task.files_locked: pause the task first, restart a completed one); an unknown index or an empty selection is 422.
patch.summary: Choose the files of a task

post.description: Appends the task at the end of the target queue.
post.summary: Move a task to another queue

post.description: Runs the task's refresh strategies (refresh.strategies) now to obtain a new link for an expired one. A refreshed task is queued again and resumes from where it stopped; when only waiting strategies remain it waits in awaiting_link. Answers 502 when no strategy produced a usable link. Running tasks must be paused first (409).

Puts a failed or awaiting_link task into the awaiting_link state: the next download the browser extension captures that matches the task's fingerprint (POST /v1/capture) becomes its new link. The wait ends after refresh.awaitTimeout.
post.summary: Wait for a new link from the browser

get.description: Every refresh step of the task: strategies that ran or were skipped, waits and their outcome, with the links before and after.

post.summary: Reorder a task within its queue

post.description: Downloads a completed or failed task again from scratch. Fails with 409 while the downloaded file exists.

get.description: The byte ranges a task downloads in parallel and how much of each is done: the data of a segments map.
Resolves Defaults ⊕ Global ⊕ Queue ⊕ Task and reports the level each value comes from.

patch.description: Replaces the task's link by hand. The new link is probed and checked against the task's fingerprint (size, strong ETag, file name): on a match the download resumes from its segments, on a mismatch onMismatch decides (409 when the link is rejected). Accepts application/json and application/merge-patch+json. Running tasks must be paused first (409).

get.description: The swarm of a torrent task: state, info hash, trackers, connected peers, bytes shared and the share ratio. Live while the task runs; otherwise what its last run saved (state stopped). 404 task.no_torrent for a task of another engine or a torrent that never ran.
Webhooks receive a signed JSON POST for the events they subscribe to. Secrets are never returned.

post.description: Delivers a webhook.test event now (one attempt, even when the webhook is disabled). Answers 502 when the endpoint does not accept it.
